abstract: Collective data support neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) arising as a resistance mechanism against anti-androgen receptor therapy. NEPC retains many of the early genomic alterations that arise in prostate adenocarcinoma but is enriched for RB1 loss. Canonically, RB1 controls cell cycle progression by binding E2F1, preventing E2F1-mediated cell cycle gene expression. Here, we show that E2F1 is overexpressed in tumors from patients with NEPC and is associated with poor prognosis. E2F1 overexpression in prostate adenocarcinoma cells correlates with the NEPC-associated transcriptional program and increases stemness, which reverts upon E2F1 depletion. E2F1 interacts and co-localizes with FOXA2 at active regulatory elements of NEPC genes and induces INSM1 expression in advanced prostate cancer, while E2F1 depletion in NEPC reduces stemness and enhances neural lineage gene expression. Altogether, we show that E2F1 plays a non-canonical role in driving NEPC-associated transcriptional changes through de-repression of REST targets and alterations to FOXA2 and ASCL1 DNA binding.
